## Work log

<!-- Chronological, written as you go. What was actually done, why, what it cost.
     Reference commits and link to plans and notes. Prose beats a checklist here —
     this is the part you will actually reread in three months. -->

- **Footprint coverage experiment (scratchpad, not committed).** Pulled four sources for the Wat Ket
  bounding box and matched each against the 1,386 OSM footprints in the Overpass cache, clipped to the
  boundary polygon by a more-than-half-inside rule. Google Open Buildings v3 (tile `30db`, level-6 S2,
  206 MB), Microsoft ML footprints (Thailand quadkey `132201300`, 36 MB), Overture 2026-08-19 buildings
  (DuckDB over S3, ~3 min), and Google Open Buildings 2.5D Temporal 2023 (two 12.5 km GeoTIFF tiles in
  EPSG:32647, read as HTTP range windows, sampled to 1 m). Bucket path gotcha: the manifest's
  `uriPrefix` ends in `…/geotiffs/3` and the tile URI starts with `0da4_…`; they concatenate with no
  slash into the S2 token `30da4`.

  | Source | Footprints in Wat Ket | Built area | OSM buildings recovered (IoU ≥ 0.3) | Polygons with no OSM counterpart |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | OSM | 1,386 | 45.5 ha | — | — |
  | Google Open Buildings v3 | 13,462 (9,860 at 80 %-precision threshold 0.738) | 177 ha | 81 % | 11,900 |
  | Microsoft | 6,317 | 145 ha | 68 % | 5,251 |
  | Overture (conflated) | 9,624 | 151 ha | 100 % (it embeds OSM) | 8,239 |

  **OSM holds roughly one building in seven.** The southern half of the district is essentially unmapped.
  Overture's primary sources for Wat Ket: 5,631 Google, 2,054 OSM, 1,939 Microsoft. Overture carries
  height for only 31 buildings, all from OSM tags.

  **Heights from the 2.5D raster are usable.** 93 % of OSM footprints have raster presence > 0.5 under
  them. Against the 57 OSM `building:levels` tags, raster mean height correlates at 0.86; the misses are
  two 10- and 12-storey tags that measure at 7 m and look like bad tags. Against the committed
  `synth.ts` heights, correlation is 0.57, median absolute error 1.6 m, but the tails are wrong in ways
  a local would notice: Rim Ping Condominium is synthesised at 8 m and measures 65 m; Embassy House is
  6.4 m vs 31 m. The raster underestimates the very tall (Supalai Monte 75 m against a 111 m tag), so
  tags should still win where present. Median heights: OSM footprints 5.6 m, Overture 4.5 m, Google
  4.6 m, so the unmapped stock is mostly one- and two-storey.
- **Adopted it the same day** — `plans/2026-09-19_satellite-footprints.plan.md`. Inside the actual
  scene clip the numbers are gentler than the whole-tambon ones: Overture holds 4,110 buildings there
  (1,184 OSM + 2,188 Google + 738 Microsoft), ~62k triangles. Built `scripts/fetch-buildings.py`
  (DuckDB → Overture parquet, rasterio range-windows → 2.5D height tif, sampling → one gitignored
  JSON cache), `src/engine/satellite.ts` (the pure merge: `overture/<id>` ids, kind `default`,
  12 m² floor, centroid-in-OSM dedupe) and an `observed` rung in `resolveHeight` between tags and
  synthesis, capped at 100 m. `fetch-osm.ts` now requires the cache or `--osm-only`.

  Result: **4,056 buildings** (google 2,143, osm 1,182, microsoft 731; 3 duplicates dropped, 70
  too small), heights observed for 76 % and synthesised for 23 %, ~61k triangles, scene document
  1,113 KB (was 462). Every OSM id, footprint, road, water and green polygon is unchanged; 972 of
  the 1,182 OSM heights moved, Rim Ping from 8 m to 65 m. All scenario and hotspot targets still
  resolve. Both scripts are byte-identical on a re-run. 293 tests and the type check pass.

  Two things bit: `buildings.ts` collided with `Buildings.tsx` on a case-insensitive filesystem
  (renamed to `satellite.ts`), and the cache bbox check needed a micro-degree of slack because the
  Python side rounds to seven decimals.
- **Extent tripled across the river** — `plans/2026-09-19_extended-extent.plan.md`. Asked for after
  the four commits landed. Costed first against Overture: the 3× rectangle (4.5 × 8.1 km, 36.5 km²)
  holds ~54,000 buildings, ~780k triangles, ~14 MB of scene; the west bank is denser than Wat Ket
  (up to 2,100 buildings per 250 m column against ~900). Raised as eight times the phone budget with
  two smaller options; the full 3× and a plain rectangular boundary were chosen. Added `--clip
  rect|tambon` and a `BUDGET` mode to `fetch-osm.ts` so the phone limits keep printing without
  rejecting. First lesson: the Overpass bbox came from the clipped ring, so the first refresh only
  covered the tambon's bbox; the clip switch had to land before the real refresh. OSM alone holds
  15,675 buildings in the rectangle — the old city is far better mapped than Wat Ket.
- **Old city, whole.** The tripled rectangle cut the moat in half. West edge pushed to −3,300 m
  (the west moat runs at about −2,880), 5.8 × 8.1 km, 47 km². The duplicate check in
  `satellite.ts` was external × OSM and stalled at 42,000 × 16,000; a 50 m grid index fixed it.
- **Relief backdrop** — `plans/2026-09-19_relief-backdrop.plan.md`. "Topography for real, so
  that when we zoom out we can see the mountains" reverses a documented non-goal, so the shape
  matters: `terrain` stays null and nothing in the baseline is draped; what is drawn is the land
  *around* the scene, from the Copernicus 30 m DEM (public COG bucket, rasterio range-reads, four
  tiles), distilled to a 256-cell field over ±24 km (187.5 m cells, 130 KB PNG + sidecar,
  byte-identical on re-run), heights 286–1,678 m with the plain at 308.4. `reliefHeights` flattens
  it under the scene rectangle at −0.3 m with a 600 m feather; `ReliefBackdrop.tsx` draws one
  unlit vertex-coloured mesh in the district group so it collapses with the district. Brand
  hypsometric ramp in `theme.ts`. Schema gains `relief` as a sibling of `region`; `validateScene`
  keeps asserting `terrain === null`. Casing trap again: `relief.ts` vs `Relief.tsx`, hence
  `ReliefBackdrop.tsx`. Copernicus requires its notice verbatim: README row and footer.
- **Result of the old-city extent:** 68,704 buildings (OSM 21,731, Google 35,391, Microsoft
  11,582), ~998k triangles, 18.8 MB scene, 9,594 roads. Both generators byte-identical.
- **The handover needed a hold.** With the relief in, zooming out shrank the district onto the
  circle before the mountains were in frame. `zoomLadder` gained `backdropOut`: the handover band
  slides down the rail so the district holds until 3× out (`RELIEF_HOLD_OUT`). Four tests.
- **Perf, and a false alarm.** The browser automation's debugger made the page take 30–100 s to
  evaluate the 15 MB chunk and slowed every merge 4–7×; in a plain Chrome tab on the static export
  the canvas renders at ~3 s and the merge takes 3.7 s. Measured by writing timings into the tab
  title and reading it back with AppleScript, which needs no debugger. Chunk parse is 0.2 s in Node.
  December's level-of-detail item should start with loading the scene as data rather than a module.
- **Bridges** — `plans/2026-09-19_bridges.plan.md`. OSM tags every Ping crossing (`bridge=yes`,
  Loi Kroh a `trestle`), 248 flagged ways in the rectangle, 48 over water. So: a generator, not
  models. `BaselineRoad.bridge` from the tag; `bridges.ts` offsets the way into a ribbon with
  bounded mitres, extends it by a ramp at each end down to ground, holds the span at a class
  height, boxes parapets along the edges and piers at a class spacing where they stand in water,
  and emits a triangle soup toned by `toneForNormal` like the buildings. 48 bridges, 3,576
  triangles, 318 ms, one mesh (`BridgeMesh.tsx` — the casing trap, third time today). 23 tests.
  Nawarat: 128 m, five piers; Nakhon Ping: 102 m, three; the Super Highway's two carriageways
  at the top of the scene. Flyovers over roads are skipped on purpose.
